key_insight: This paper shows that an AI system can act like an autonomous X-ray scientist, aligning single crystals at a real synchrotron beamline without constant human intervention. It demonstrates how large language models can drive adaptive, closed-loop experiments in a complex scientific facility.
problem_solved: Traditional synchrotron experiments often require expert operators to manually align samples and adjust procedures in real time. The paper addresses the challenge of automating this high-precision, decision-heavy experimental workflow.
method: Built an agentic AI workflow that uses a large language model to plan and adapt experimental actions.
Connected the AI to a real synchrotron beamline so it can autonomously align single crystals and respond to experimental feedback.
Used closed-loop control, where observations from the beamline inform the next action, enabling iterative self-correction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this is a strong example of LLMs moving beyond text into real-world scientific control systems. It highlights the potential of agentic AI for automating expert workflows, improving experimental throughput, and enabling new forms of autonomous discovery.
visual_elements: A closed-loop workflow diagram showing AI decision-making, beamline actions, and feedback from measurements.
A simplified beamline illustration with crystal sample alignment highlighted.
Before/after graphic comparing manual alignment vs autonomous AI alignment.
An icon-based sequence for sensing, reasoning, acting, and updating.
paper_title: An agentic artificially intelligent X-ray scientist
paper_authors: Zhantao Chen, Alexander N. Petsch, Aidan J. Israelski, Rajan Plumley, Lingjia Shen
